name: IEEE CASS Hackathon 2026
description: A 24-hour national-level hackathon organized by the IEEE Circuits and Systems Society. Tackle real-world engineering challenges across two focused domains.

timeline.description: Portal opens on Unstop. Form your team and register early.
Last date to register. No entries accepted after this.
Opening ceremony followed by problem statement reveal and hacking sprint.
All prototypes, documentation, and presentations must be submitted.
Expert panel reviews and scores all submissions against defined criteria.
Winners are announced at the closing ceremony with prize distribution.

faq.question: Who can participate?
faq.answer: The hackathon is open to all undergraduate and postgraduate engineering students from recognized institutions across India. Participants must be current IEEE student members or willing to register as one.

faq.question: What is the team size?
faq.answer: Teams must consist of 2 to 4 members. Solo registrations are not accepted. All team members must be from the same institution unless special permission is granted by the organizing committee.

faq.question: Is there a registration fee?
faq.answer: Registration is completely free for all IEEE student members. Non-members can register by becoming an IEEE student member, which carries a nominal annual fee.

faq.question: How are submissions evaluated?
faq.answer: Submissions are evaluated on four parameters: technical innovation (30%), problem relevance (25%), prototype completeness (25%), and presentation clarity (20%). A panel of industry and academic experts conducts the evaluation.

faq.question: Are beginners allowed?
faq.answer: Absolutely. The hackathon is designed to be inclusive. Beginners are encouraged to participate and will have access to pre-event workshops, mentors throughout the event, and guidance sessions from senior IEEE members.

faq.question: What resources are provided during the hackathon?
faq.answer: Participants will have access to cloud credits, development toolkits, datasets relevant to the problem statements, meals, and 24-hour technical support from mentors.
